claims.explanation: HA14-1 is a small-molecule Bcl-2 inhibitor that occupies the BH3-binding pocket and prevents Bcl-2 from sequestering pro-apoptotic Bax, so lines that depend on high BCL2 (or BCL2-family) anti-apoptotic tone for survival are expected to be selectively killed. The pattern is best explained by BCL2/BCL2A1/BCL2L1 expression and by loss of the pro-apoptotic effectors that mediate the response (BAX/BAK1), rather than by any single lineage or common driver mutation.

features.basis: HA14-1 binds the Bcl-2 surface pocket and induces apoptosis in Bcl-2-overexpressing cells; Bcl-2 knockdown abolishes HA14-1 sensitization
HA14-1 sensitization is lost when cells express a Bax mutant that cannot interact with Bcl-2
Bcl-xL can substitute for Bcl-2 in suppressing apoptosis and is not the HA14-1 target
other anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family members create the same BH3-mimetic-sensitive apoptotic block
hTERT overexpression blocks HA14-1-induced apoptosis independently of telomerase activity
HA14-1 kills via a p53-independent mitochondrial/caspase-9 route, so TP53 loss does not protect and is common in sensitive lines
BH3 mimetics engage Beclin 1-dependent autophagy; Beclin1 knockdown diminishes cell death
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, NCIH1648) are among the most killed
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (IGR37, K029AX) appear in the sensitive set
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines (786O, ZR751, FTC133)
KRAS-mutant colorectal/pancreatic lines (SNUC5, T3M4, OV7) are enriched among least-affected lines
NF1-mutant lines appear in both sets but several least-affected lines carry NF1 loss
